editorial.description_en: Earth taken past bisque. The most saturated entry in the group and the reddest.
editorial.description_ja: 強く焼いた土のような、いちばん赤い色。
editorial.contemporaryNote_en: The accent in the Earth and Clay palette. It is the one member that cannot be used as a ground, and putting it beside a neutral is what the palette is for.

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.544, C 0.102, h 42.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 焼き (yaki, firing) + 土 (tsuchi, earth). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Fired Earth" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 焼土. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — sabi-suna at ΔE00 5.1, mi-aka at ΔE00 8.3, chiri-ba at ΔE00 8.5. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (222°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
